clue.text: The girl Eliza at last, fancy product of refinement

indicators.note: fancy, as an adjective meaning elaborate or contrived, tells us to rework the letters
at last points to the final letter of the name Eliza

explanation.surface: Eliza Doolittle's polished new manner is a fancy result of her refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives A, the end of Eliza; 'fancy' rearranges THEGIRL plus A. The surface steers you to Eliza Doolittle's social refining, but the definition is metallurgical.
explanation.definitionFit: Litharge, lead monoxide, is formed as a by-product when silver is refined from lead ores.

clue.text: Prepared to engage e.g. Middle Temple for reviewing court action

indicators.note: reviewing is looking back over, so the whole built word is read in the opposite direction
to engage means to take something in, so one word holds another inside it

parts.note: set means prepared, ready
Middle Temple is one of the Inns of Court, the London legal societies

explanation.surface: A barrister ready to take on a Middle Temple case reviews the court proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reviewing' turns round SINNET, the container step's result. The legal surface makes 'court action' look like litigation, but it means play on a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is played on a court, so it is literally the action that happens there.

clue.text: The Almighty against mediating command to restore extinct beast

indicators.note: mediating means standing in the middle between two parties, so these pieces go in the middle of another word

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to let deleted text stand, so it restores it
God is the Almighty
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: God's intervention against a command brings an extinct animal back.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet is the proof-reader's mark meaning 'let it stand', written beside a deletion to cancel it, hence a command to restore.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegodont was a prehistoric elephant-like mammal, now long extinct.

clue.text: Spouses left transfixed by Northern Lights

indicators.note: transfixed by means pierced through, so one letter is driven into the middle of a word

parts.note: widows are wives left behind when their husbands die

explanation.surface: Bereaved wives stand spellbound by the Northern Lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Lights' reads as the aurora, but Northern gives only N and Lights is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights is an old word for the glazed openings of a building, its panes and windows.

clue.text: Man at party given by English Theatre

parts.note: a stag is a man at a stag party, the all-male night out before a wedding

explanation.surface: An Englishman at a stag party is given tickets for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage is the theatre as a profession or art form, as in a career on the stage.

clue.text: Bear gardens when relocating lead to early dismissals

parts.note: heave means to lift and carry something heavy, to bear it

indicators.note: relocating means moving something away from where it was, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: hoes is a verb meaning gardens, works soil with a hoe

indicators.note: lead to here means the leading letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Gardeners at a bear pit lift and move things before getting sacked early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead to early' is E, the first letter of 'early'; 'when relocating' moves it out of HEAVEHOES, leaving HEAVEHOS. 'Bear gardens' looks like the historic bear-baiting arenas.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the heave-ho is slang for being thrown out or sacked, so heave-hos are dismissals.

clue.text: Obsessive until getting in without a key

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: anal is slang for fussily obsessive
to can mean until, as in nine to five

explanation.surface: Someone obsessive waits until they can get in, having lost their key.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a locked-out person; the definition is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written with no tonal centre, that is, not in any key.

clue.text: Survive burning

definitions.meaning: to survive is to go on living
... coals are still alight and burning

explanation.definitionFit: Survive and stay alive are synonyms, and live as an adjective means glowing and on fire.

clue.text: There it is dancing in the nude, like the king in a suit?

definitions.text: like the king in a suit?

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order
nude means stripped bare, so the words lose their outer letters and only the inside remains

explanation.surface: Someone sees a naked dancer, as bare as an emperor in his new clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges THEREIT into THIRTEE; 'nude' strips 'in the' to NTH. The question mark flags the playing-card sense of 'suit'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a suit of playing cards, ace to king, the king is card number thirteen.

clue.text: Loop work is new inlay for tabard, I'm relieved to say

indicators.note: a new inlay replaces the existing middle of a garment, so the middle of the word is swapped out

parts.note: a hank is a coiled loop of yarn or rope
go means work, as in the engine won't go

explanation.surface: Embroidering loops into a tabard as a new decoration, the maker sighs with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner letters ABAR of 'tabard' are replaced by HANK plus GO, leaving T and D at the edges. A tabard is a sleeveless tunic worn by heralds.
explanation.definitionFit: Thank God is an exclamation of relief, said when a worry has passed.

clue.text: Liberal government's initial subsistence is pounds short

indicators.note: initial points to the first letter of the word government
short means lacking, so the word goes without one letter

parts.note: a living is one's means of subsistence
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Liberal government's first step is to cut subsistence payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital pretends to be the party, but it is the adjective meaning generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person is generous, open-handed, always ready to hand things out.

clue.text: Carpet order after discount

parts.note: to dress ranks is to put soldiers in order, aligning them
after a discount a price is down, reduced

explanation.surface: Someone buys a carpet once the price has been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering but is the verb meaning to reprimand, as when an employee is called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them, to give them a telling-off or reprimand.

clue.text: Outside of school, finally rebuked kid

indicators.note: outside of tells us one word wraps around another

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, meaning rebuked

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word school

explanation.surface: Outside school, a kid finally gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: CHID goes around L, the end of 'school'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is informal for a youngster, a son or daughter.

clue.text: Most charity boxes nothing of great consequence

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, as in a box, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
O looks like zero, nothing
tall means large and imposing, so something tall is of great size and weight

explanation.surface: Most charity collecting boxes hold nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like the collecting tins of the surface, but it is the container signal; 'Most' at the front is the definition, not an adjective on charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Most and nearly every one mean the same proportion, the great majority.

clue.text: Sense growth in Spooner's gardening business?

annotationWithheld.why: Sense growth in Spooner's gardening business? (7): no Spoonerism of a gardening business giving FEELING could be found, and the blog does not explain it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sense growth in Spooner's gardening business?

clue.text: Look after client, badly wanting a drop of Taylor's Landlord

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
badly means in a jumbled, poor way, so the letters are rearranged
a drop of means just a little bit, here the first letter of the word Taylor's

parts.note: see means look

explanation.surface: A publican looks after a customer who badly wants a drop of Timothy Taylor's Landlord ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters left when T, 'a drop of Taylor's', is taken from the clue's word, giving LICEN. Timothy Taylor's Landlord is a well-known Yorkshire bitter, so the definition hides in a beer name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord holds the alcohol licence, so is the licence holder of the premises.

clue.text: Extremely thorough KC loses two cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, as a case holds something, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A thorough King's Counsel nonetheless loses two cases.
explanation.walkthrough: KC is a King's Counsel, a senior barrister; the surface's legal 'cases' are really containers.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest scrutiny is the most searching and detailed, so closest means most thorough.

clue.text: Perhaps accepting beard that's so lovely cut off by surgeon?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: say means perhaps or for instance
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley
aw is the cooing exclamation for something sweet

explanation.surface: A lovely beard is perhaps lopped off by a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' opens the outer word after its first letter. The definition is loose: a surgeon's saw takes a limb off, so the question mark signals the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon amputating a limb saws through it, so the limb is removed with a saw.

clue.text: In lift when accosted by drunk, Tom flips

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift means raised up, so the built word reads from bottom to top
accosted by means approached and hemmed in, so one word stands inside the other

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a tom is a male cat, and puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Tom, pestered by a drunk in a lift, loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when accosted by' gives SPUSSOT, and 'In lift' reverses it. The surface 'flips' means loses one's temper; the definition is coin tosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip is a toss-up, a decision left to chance.

clue.text: Angry driver, yet to pass test, again bottles it

indicators.note: bottles means keeps something sealed inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: back can mean again, as in back to square one
L stands for a learner driver, from the L-plates they display

explanation.surface: A furious learner driver loses their nerve on a second attempt at the test.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK holds L. 'bottles it' is British slang for losing one's nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A black mood or black look is an angry one.

clue.text: Being plied with champagne maybe makes insensitive type amorous

indicators.note: plied with means filled up with drink, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a log is a person who feels nothing, as in sleep like a log
champagne is a French wine, vin in French

explanation.surface: Plying a cold fish with champagne turns them romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: LOG holds VIN; 'maybe' shows champagne is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving and amorous both describe someone feeling affection and romance.

clue.text: Future domestics? After another couple, we separately will depart

indicators.note: the two letters leave the phrase from two different places, not side by side
after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: two more is another couple
a domestic is British slang for a household quarrel, a row
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple wonder whether future rows will drive them apart.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO MORE ROWS loses W (from TWO) and E (from MORE). 'Domestics' as a noun means household rows in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: One's tomorrows are the days ahead, the time to come, so the noun matches futures.

clue.text: Even this one-off would fluster veterinary

indicators.note: to fluster is to throw into confusion, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Something unique enough to rattle even a vet.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of VETERINARY are EVEN plus the answer, rearranged: 'this' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something seldom found, a unique or singular item.

clue.text: The dark horse on board, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the knight is the chess piece shaped like a horse

explanation.surface: A dark horse appears on the board, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark horse' runs together in the surface but splits between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness after sunset.

clue.text: Back Parisian goes, opposing forward at the San Siro?

indicators.note: back means going in the reverse direction, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: va is French for goes
anti means opposing

explanation.surface: A Parisian back goes up against an Italian forward at Milan's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The San Siro is AC and Inter Milan's football stadium; 'back' and 'forward' look like football positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Avanti is Italian for onward or go ahead, the shout of a crowd urging a team on.

clue.text: Black gram integral to one Asian meal time

indicators.note: integral to means forming part of the whole, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: satay is a Southeast Asian dish of grilled skewered meat
urd is the black gram bean used in Indian cookery

explanation.surface: Black gram is a key ingredient at an Asian dinner time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black gram' looks like a weight but is a pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday is a day of the week, a period on the calendar.

clue.text: A New College do, lecturer's first, outside part of college building

parts.note: a tech is a technical college
to ape is to do, as in do an impression of

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word lecturer's

explanation.surface: At a New College function, a lecturer speaks first outside the building.
explanation.walkthrough: New College is an Oxford college, a deliberate red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An antechapel is the outer vestibule at the west end of a college chapel.

clue.text: Which Astaire musical omits something performed in theatre?

indicators.note: omits means leaves out, so these letters are dropped from the title

parts.note: Top Hat is the 1935 Fred Astaire film musical
an op, an operation, is performed in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A question about which Astaire musical leaves something out of its stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but is an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Which and that are interchangeable relative pronouns introducing a clause.
